description: Platinum is a dense, malleable, ductile, highly unreactive, precious, silverish-white transition metal with atomic number 78 and symbol Pt. It is a member of the platinum group of elements and group 10 of the periodic table, with six naturally occurring isotopes. One of the rarer elements in Earth's crust with an average abundance of approximately 5 μg/kg, it is highly valuable as a major precious metal commodity.
uses: Platinum is a key component in catalytic converters, laboratory equipment, electrical contacts and electrodes, platinum resistance thermometers, dentistry equipment, and jewelry. It is used in the glass industry to manipulate molten glass, and platinum compounds such as cisplatin, oxaliplatin and carboplatin are applied in chemotherapy as treatment for certain types of cancer. Hexachloroplatinic acid serves as a precursor for many platinum compounds and has applications in photography, zinc etchings, indelible ink, plating, mirrors, and porcelain coloring.
characteristics: Platinum is lustrous, ductile, and malleable, being the most ductile of pure metals and more ductile than gold, silver or copper. It does not corrode and bulk platinum does not oxidize in air at any temperature, making it a noble metal. Its most common oxidation states are +2 and +4, and although generally unreactive, it is attacked by chlorine, bromine, iodine, sulfur, and fluorine, and dissolves in hot aqua regia.
